items.text: A video sent to Iran International shows a classroom fire at Bandar Mahshahr University on Sunday, 17 Aban.

Today, Sunday, a group of Social Security retirees held a gathering in front of the organization's building in Rasht, demanding an increase in payments in line with inflation, equalization of salaries, removal of Social Security from government monopoly, and resolution of supplementary insurance issues to improve their medical services.

Ali Sadrazadeh, a Middle East analyst, said that although the Houthis are not militarily capable of confronting Saudi Arabia, even limited attacks and minor damages caused by them can affect Saudi Arabia's economy due to symbolic and psychological consequences.

Simultaneously with the formation of a special US task force to expand the economic siege of Iran, the Iraqi Foreign Minister announced the closure of all border crossings of his country with Iran, except for two crossings. The spokesperson of the IRGC called the Iron Gate plan a "play on words." Mahtab Gholizadeh commented on the impact of the new CENTCOM campaign on Iran's imports and exports.
Fouad Qaderi, a citizen from Javanrud, was released from Dizelabad Prison in Kermanshah on Saturday, 16 Aban, after posting bail.

Hossein Taeb, head of the Basij Organization, said that in coordination with the Ministries of Oil and Energy and the Gas Company, they have obtained a list of high consumers and trained 150,000 Basij members as energy helpers to promote energy saving. He added that devoted members will participate in this plan and a drill on energy saving will be conducted. Taeb also said that energy saving can improve people's livelihoods and everyone must make sacrifices.

Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum announced that despite many economic and political challenges, the UAE's foreign trade in the first 9 months of 2026 grew by 10 percent compared to last year, nearing about three trillion dirhams. He added that exports to the UAE's 10 largest trading partners increased by 31 percent compared to last year.

The CEO of Mazandaran Water and Wastewater Company announced that 151 villages and 44 cities in the province are facing water stress and problems in providing drinking water. Behzad Bararzadeh emphasized that the multi-fold increase in population during peak travel times puts additional pressure on the water supply network, and resolving existing problems requires more funding.

A bus carrying members of the Sahar Academy basketball team overturned near Shush while returning from Abadan to Tehran. The team supervisor stated that the players' general condition is stable, although some were injured and a few suffered fractures. Additionally, in a minibus accident in Van province, Turkey, 9 people died and 5 were injured, with some victims being Iranian citizens.

Ali Belali, advisor to the commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force, said that the necessary arms reserves for the country's defense have been secured for years and the armed forces are ready and on trigger. He added that the armed forces are waiting for an opportunity to give the enemy an unforgettable lesson. Belali also said the enemy is old and worn out and lacks the military capability to confront Iran.

Messages received by Iran International in response to the execution of three young people in Karaj reflect the anger, sorrow, and concern of citizens about the continuation of executions in Iran. Audiences expressed concern over the silence of the international community and the actions of the United States, emphasizing the need to continue seeking justice and to end executions and the rule of the Islamic Republic.

In anti-government protests in Tirana on Saturday, 16 Aban, protesters threw stones at police and set trash bins on fire, demanding the resignation of Edi Rama. Police used water cannons to disperse the protesters. These protests began in May opposing the construction of a luxury hotel in a protected area.

The Director General of Natural Resources and Watershed Management of Kurdistan reported the issuance of 133 green and alternative prison sentences for offenders in cases of encroachment and destruction of national lands in this province since the beginning of the current year. The convicts have been obliged to plant more than seven thousand saplings and undertake other actions such as providing equipment for the protection of natural resources and supplying stationery for underprivileged students.

European security and intelligence agencies are investigating the possibility of groups linked to Russia being involved in a widespread wave of bomb threats against passenger flights in European countries.
On Friday, 15 Aban, a fuel transporter was injured after military forces fired at his vehicle on the Mirjaveh to Zahedan route.

The Gulf Cooperation Council and the countries of Jordan, Bahrain, and Qatar called for an end to missile and drone attacks by the Houthis supported by the Islamic Republic on Saudi Arabia. The council and the foreign ministries of these three countries condemned the attacks on Riyadh and southern Saudi Arabia, including an attempt to target an Aramco administrative building. The Secretary-General of the Gulf Cooperation Council described these attacks as "cowardly terrorist acts" and called for decisive international action to stop them.

Hailstorm on Sunday, 17 Aban caused flooding in the streets of Kermanshah; the city's streets turned into rivers of water and hail. Images of the strong flow of water and hail in Kermanshah streets have been published.

Israel Katz, Israel's defense minister, said Tehran is taking actions that could be dangerous for Israel as it resumes its nuclear program. He added that Israel is united against threats from the Islamic Republic despite different political tendencies.

The Virgol platform announced the blocking of its international domain. Previously, the international domains of Varzesh3 and Tetherland were also blocked and transferred to national domains. Iman Samiizadeh says transferring Iranian commercial domains to national domains can endanger the security of users and website administrators.

The head of education in District 2 of Rey County reported a shortage of educational space and the need to build eight new schools in the area. He said that despite about 49,000 students studying, some densely populated neighborhoods face a shortage of schools and high student density. Four schools are under construction, but this number does not meet the needs, and building eight more schools is necessary.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, announced on Sunday, 17 Aban that the recent election results were a major setback for America. He wrote that the stock market lost three trillion dollars in value in one day. Trump added that they will return stronger than ever.

The police commander of Fuman reported the closure of four cafe-restaurants in this county due to what was called "violation of norms and non-observance of Islamic proprieties." The operators of these business units have been referred to judicial authorities.

Ali Babaei Karnami, head of the parliamentary social commission, stated that about eight million people in Iran have fallen into absolute poverty and malnutrition due to the improper implementation of the preferential currency removal plan, and up to 50 million others face difficulties obtaining necessary food. He said the plan was supposed to provide subsidies at the end of the distribution chain after removing the 28,500 toman currency so that people could still buy essential goods at subsidized prices. Babaei Karnami added that access to food has become so difficult for a large part of Iran's population that they cannot get enough daily calories.

On Sunday, 17 Aban, reports of the execution of three young men in Karaj were published, and various reactions were seen on social media. Some expressed concern about the destruction of infrastructure by the Islamic Republic, while others criticized the executions. There were also calls for the overthrow of the government and an end to executions.

Seyed Mohammad Pakmehr, a member of the Health and Treatment Commission of the Parliament, reported a shortage of 320 hospital beds in North Khorasan province. Seyed Ahmad Hashemi, head of the provincial University of Medical Sciences, stated that out of 120 beds needed for psychiatric patients, only 60 beds are active. He also pointed to the aging building of Imam Reza Hospital and the lack of treatment space as obstacles in providing services to psychiatric and pediatric patients.

People inside Iran reacted to the gathering of Iranians in Frankfurt on 16 Aban, describing it as a source of hope and light in their hearts. Messages from Mashhad, Nishapur, Kazeroon, and Isfahan expressed support for Prince Reza Pahlavi and gratitude to the participants. Some statements referred to resistance against repression and hope for Iran's freedom.
A video sent to Iran International shows flooding in the streets of Gorgan after rainfall on Sunday, 17 Aban.

According to a report by the UK Maritime Trade Operations published on Sunday, 17 Aban, two attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz were recorded in the past 72 hours. The report also indicates a decrease in the number of attacks from four to two. One tanker reported an explosion on its hull while exiting the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, 14 Aban, and another tanker was targeted by an unknown projectile on Saturday, 16 Aban.

On Saturday, 16 Aban, seven citizens named Adel Othmani, Sultan Othmani, Aziz Ghargholi, Ali Heydari, Mohsen Salihavi, Ali Salihavi, and Tehran Othmani were arrested by Intelligence Department forces in Bandar Mahshahr and transferred to an unknown location. These individuals reside in Saadi neighborhood of Bandar Mahshahr. The Harana news agency reported these arrests.

Prince Reza Pahlavi said in an interview with a German journalist that the fall of the Islamic Republic is certain and totalitarian regimes eventually fall. He added that international support can accelerate the process of change and reduce the costs for the Iranian people. Pahlavi also said that any action weakening the regime's tools of repression would be welcomed by the people and described such actions as humanitarian intervention.

Kambiz Tavana spoke in an interview with Mark Katz about the impact of recent wars between Israel and the US with the Islamic Republic on Tehran-Moscow relations and the extent of Russia's influence on the Iranian government's decisions.

The head of the Environmental Protection Department of Shahr-e Qods announced the issuance of a green sentence for an environmental offender. According to this sentence, the person responsible for an unauthorized waste sorting center was sentenced to plant 30 saplings and maintain and water them for three months.

Heavy rain and flooding on Sunday, 17 Aban caused widespread waterlogging of streets in parts of Bushehr and Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad provinces, disrupting citizens' movement. In Khormoj, the center of Dashti County in Bushehr province, floods covered streets and traffic routes. Published images show the severity of waterlogging and flooding in the streets.

Gadi Eisenkot, tasked with forming the Israeli government, announced that the war fronts remain open and the war goals have not been achieved. He said Israel has no time for delay or consecutive elections and must form an emergency national government as soon as possible. Eisenkot emphasized that the security and political challenges are urgent and parties must participate in forming the new government as soon as possible.

Today, Shahou Ebrahimi, a resident of Baneh city, was arrested after appearing at the enforcement branch of the Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office of this city to serve a seven-month prison sentence and was transferred to Baneh prison.

Iran International obtained a confidential document of the deputy oil minister's response to Ali Shamkhani's letter to Ali Khamenei, indicating that Hossein Shamkhani has held the monopoly on Iran's oil sales in the UAE for a long time and, after purchasing a ship with an Iranian government loan, transports Russian oil.

On Sunday, 17 Aban, the sky of Qazvin witnessed the formation of unusually shaped clouds coinciding with the arrival of a rain system. Published images show changes in the shape and color of the sky ahead of the rain system's activity.

Cristiano Ronaldo, after retiring from the Portuguese national team, began his official cinema experience by producing the action-comedy film "Stuntnats." The film stars Chris Hemsworth, Sam Rockwell, and Matt Damon, and tells the story of two professional stuntmen who take on a Hollywood project to save their local sports club. The film is directed by Damian Walters and features several famous Hollywood stunt performers.

Al Hadath network reported that an Iraqi delegation made an eight-hour trip to Tehran, met with Islamic Republic officials, and delivered a message from the United States. This trip followed a phone call between Donald Trump and Ali Al-Zaidi and a visit by Tom Barrack to Baghdad.

The detention order for Seyed Mohammad Saleh Hosseini, Mohammad Hakimpoor, Mostafa Ghaderi, Khaled Rahimi, and Hossein Abdollahi, five citizens from Saqez who are held in the county prison, was extended for another month.
A DJ in Tehran was arrested by order of the city's prosecutor for holding mixed-gender parties. His Instagram page was also blocked by judicial order.

At the end of the twelfth week of the Iranian Premier League, Sepahan reached the top of the table with 26 points. Persepolis, Tractor, and Foolad each have 23 points, and Esteghlal follows with 21 points. Malavan and Sanat Naft Abadan are at the bottom of the table, and Mes Shahrbabak remains the only team without a win this season.

Nechirvan Barzani, the President of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, met in Erbil with a delegation from the Islamic Republic led by Mohammadreza Mesgariyan, responsible for the Kurdistan Region file in the IRGC, and discussed security cooperation, bilateral agreements, and regional stability. According to a statement from the Kurdistan Region presidency, the two sides reviewed relations between Iraq and the Kurdistan Region with the Islamic Republic and ways to expand cooperation in various fields. Barzani and the Islamic Republic delegation also emphasized the use of dialogue and peaceful diplomatic solutions to resolve problems and tensions.

Videos received by Iran International show that a group of Iranians residing in Germany on Sunday, 17 Aban, set up a tent with images of martyrs in front of the US Consulate General in Dusseldorf and, placing a doll of Khamenei on the ground, danced beside it for the death of the dictator of Iran.

Araghchi said American voters have made their choice, and now it is time for the White House to make its choice. He maintained his two-day proposal, which includes ending the war on all fronts. Araghchi warned that if war is chosen, their vigilant and seasoned warriors will unleash hell on their enemies.

A 20-year-old worker died after falling from a height in Shandiz. It was reported that the worker fell while installing the roof and constructing a warehouse in a building under construction in Shandiz.

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, wrote on Sunday, 17 Aban, on Network X, addressing the White House to choose war and witness how Iran's ready and seasoned forces bring hell upon them. He said American voters have made their choice, and now it is the White House's turn. Araghchi added that Iran's two-day offer to end the war on all fronts still stands.

Asieh Aryanfar, a lawyer, spoke about shootings at kolbars in the western border areas of Iran and the difficulties in judicial follow-up. She discussed shooting regulations, the responsibility of officers, the performance of the border incident commission, and the issuance of non-prosecution orders. Aryanfar also referred to the practice of some courts declaring kolbars' blood as "wasted" and the need to reform the weapon use law.

Hossein Mohseni, spokesperson for the IRGC, said if the US is serious about enforcing an economic blockade against the Islamic Republic, "we are even more serious." He added that the US predictions about the economic collapse of the regime did not happen and certainly will not happen.

The Disciplinary Committee of the Football Federation has summoned Yaser Asani, Esteghlal Tehran player, and Shoja Khalilzadeh, Tractor player, along with the head and cultural officer of the Tractor club. They must appear before the committee on Wednesday. Esteghlal club believes the main cause of the tension was the assistant referee and has requested the release of the refereeing team's conversations for clarification.

Workers of the National Industrial Steel Group in Ahvaz complain about delays in wage payments, non-payment of October salaries, removal of production benefits, stopping meal provisions, and not receiving work clothes. They demand the restart of production lines and timely payment of wages.

Isaac Herzog, President of Israel, invited Gadi Eizenkot to form the next government of Israel. Eizenkot's party received fewer votes than Netanyahu's Likud party in the parliamentary elections, but 67 members of the Knesset supported him to form the government. Eizenkot has a maximum of 6 weeks to form the government and then receive a vote of confidence from the Knesset.

The death sentences of two prisoners convicted in a joint murder case were carried out in Sepidar Prison in Ahvaz. Additionally, two prisoners sentenced to death in Abbasabad and Chaldoran were spared from execution with the consent of the victims' families.

Abolfazl Qadyani, an 81-year-old political prisoner, was sentenced in absentia to two years in prison by Branch 29 of Tehran Revolutionary Court. The sentence was issued on charges including "propaganda against the regime" and "insulting the Supreme Leader" in a case opened against him during his imprisonment. The sentence was communicated to him last week in prison.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, stated on Sunday, 17 Aban, that if negotiations to end the conflicts progress, the likelihood of ordering new attacks against Iran will be very low. Al Arabiya and Al Hadath media reported an 8-hour visit by an Iraqi delegation to Iran delivering a message from the White House to Tehran officials.
Sahand Nikkhah, a 16-year-old teenager and student living in Ilam, was released from the city's prison after 23 days of detention upon posting bail.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad, on the "Cheshm Andaz" program, strongly criticized IRIB documentaries and said that government media distort the reality of the Dey protests by portraying protesters as armed and trained for a coup. Pointing to the contradiction between the accusations and the broadcast images, he considered forced confessions invalid. Mahdavi-Azad rejected attributing accusations of terrorism and coup to the protesters and strongly criticized the Islamic Republic's efforts to justify their killing and execution.

Before the US naval blockade, about 80% of Iran's trade was conducted through southern ports. After the blockade, the Islamic Republic tried to transfer part of the exchanges to alternative borders. CENTCOM recently announced that it will extend the blockade regarding sanctioned, military, and dual-use goods to land borders and the Caspian Sea.

Carlos Alcaraz won the Paris Masters by defeating American Ben Shelton in two sets, securing his ninth Masters 1000 title. Alcaraz became the first Spanish tennis player since David Ferrer in 2012 to win this tournament. After his sixth attempt, he said this is something he has worked hard to achieve for a long time.

At least 4 protest gatherings were held. Social Security retirees protested in Ahvaz, Rasht, and Shush in front of Social Security Organization buildings. The strike of private bus drivers in Yazd entered its eighth day.

Axios reported that Donald Trump, the President of the United States, on Thursday, 14 Aban, had a phone call with Benjamin Netanyahu, the Prime Minister of Israel, asking him to take actions to implement the "Gaza Peace Plan." The plan includes disarming Hamas, demilitarizing the Gaza Strip, and handing over its administration to a new Palestinian government. The plan's implementation had been paused due to Israeli elections and will be gradual, with Gaza's reconstruction starting only after progress in disarming Hamas is confirmed.
A video received by Iran International shows chanting of the slogan "Long live the Shah" in a classroom of a school in Yasuj city.

Several messages received from 22:22 report explosion sounds in Bandar Mahshahr. Some people heard two explosions at 22:20. Later messages suggest the sound might have been from an electrical transformer bursting.
Saeed Shahbakhsh, Naser Shahbakhsh, and Saeed Shahbakhsh, three citizens from Taftan county, remain in uncertainty in Zahedan prison after 104 days of detention.

Erfan Ghanei-Fard, a Middle East analyst, said Prince Reza Pahlavi's statements about the certainty of the Islamic Republic's fall emphasize the link between three factors: erosion of repression capacity, collapse of political legitimacy, and rupture in the cohesion of the government's command structure. He added that weakening the Islamic Republic's military power alone does not guarantee regime change, and the combination of external pressure, internal action, and the presence of a trusted political alternative can determine the transition path.

Hassan Mansour, an economist, referred to reports about absolute poverty and malnutrition in Iran and said that war, sanctions, and disruptions in the production and distribution chain of food have intensified the livelihood crisis, but the main root of this situation should be sought in the system of resource and income distribution in the Islamic Republic.
Four severe explosions occurred in Qeshm at 22:45. These explosions happened consecutively.

Harana news agency reported that Mohammad Mahdi Parsa, detained during the protests of Dey 1404 and held in Sheiban prison in Ahvaz, has been sentenced to death for "Moharebeh" and to a total of 20 years in prison for two other charges. His sentence was issued on 11 Aban 1405 by the Revolutionary Court of Ahvaz. Parsa was denied access to a lawyer of his choice during the trial.

Amir Ghalenoei announced the new Iran national football team list for the matches against Iraq and Palestine. Names such as Mehdi Taremi, Shoja Khalilzadeh, Ehsan Hajsafi, and Saman Ghoddos are not included. The coaching staff stated that Alireza Beiranvand was not invited due to injury, and the federation emphasized that this decision does not mean a change in the status of experienced players in future plans.

IRNA news agency reported on the evening of Sunday, 17 Aban, that points on Qeshm Island were hit. The Telegram channel Vahid Online, citing its audience, reported four severe explosions in Qeshm. Fars news agency announced that explosion sounds were heard on Qeshm Island and Bandar Abbas.

Houshang Hassan-Yari, a Middle East and military affairs expert, said the Islamic Republic uses Yemen's Houthis as a tool to pressure Saudi Arabia, the UAE, the US, and Israel. He added that Tehran's goal in these attacks is to increase pressure on regional countries and gain leverage in the war with the US. Hassan-Yari also said that attacks on Saudi oil facilities could raise global energy prices and have broad economic and political consequences.

Tasnim reported, citing a knowledgeable source, that the sound of three shots was heard from the Sirik area towards the Strait of Hormuz. The state media announced that these shots were related to an encounter with unauthorized vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.

The human rights group Halvash reported the formation of long queues of heavy vehicles at the Rimdan border crossing on the Iran-Pakistan border. Drivers complain about disorder in the queue system, lack of welfare facilities, and the risk of spoilage of fruit and vegetable shipments. They say this situation causes significant financial losses.

Tasnim News Agency, affiliated with the IRGC, confirmed reports of an attack on Qeshm Island by the United States early Monday, 18 Aban. Earlier, IRNA reported strikes on points in Qeshm. Additionally, Vahid Online and Fars News Agency reported severe explosions and hearing explosion sounds in Qeshm, Mahshahr, and Bandar Abbas.

The football match between Esteghlal Khuzestan and Esteghlal in the twelfth week of the Premier League ended in a 2-2 draw. The match was overshadowed by controversial behavior and the expulsion of Yaser Asani. This match was one of the spectacular matches of the twelfth week.

Donald Trump announced that the special forces operation "Iron Gate" in Iran is being carried out with full force. He said that alongside the largest naval blockade in history, almost nothing enters or leaves Iran. Trump emphasized the continuation of this operation and the naval blockade of Iran.

Mohammad Taghavi said in the Hattrick program that the match between Esteghlal Khuzestan and Esteghlal was one of the most spectacular games in recent years of Iranian football. He added that Yaser Asani was clearly tired due to the congestion of matches and could not even run in the final minutes.

A group of Social Security retirees in Rasht gathered on Sunday, 17 Aban, to protest the neglect of their demands and the violation of their rights. The protesters chanted slogans in support of political prisoners and the cancellation of death sentences.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that Trump's two-month window for attacking the Islamic Republic is passing and the US is strengthening its military posture in the region. The aircraft carrier Roosevelt has left Singapore and entered the Malacca Strait and is estimated to reach the CENTCOM area within seven to ten days. The amphibious group Makin Island has also left Japan and is heading towards the Middle East, carrying stealth F-35 fighters.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that simultaneously with the movement of the aircraft carrier Roosevelt and its accompanying strike group towards the CENTCOM command area, the amphibious assault group "Makin Island" along with two other ships and 2,200 marines has left Japan heading to the CENTCOM area. This group is equipped with stealth F-35 fighters and is essentially a different type of aircraft carrier with an amphibious assault mission.

Mike Huckabee, the US ambassador to Israel, said he does not know what decision Donald Trump will make regarding a possible attack on the Islamic Republic and that he might only be informed at the start of the attack or upon hearing the first siren. Huckabee said the proposal to gradually reduce US aid to Israel was initially raised by Benjamin Netanyahu, and the current aid agreement still has two years of validity. He added that such an action would likely require a decision by Congress.

Sky News Arabia reported that the Prime Minister of Iraq has ordered an investigation into the drone attack on the Khurmor gas field in Sulaymaniyah province. The attack on Sunday, 17 Aban, hit gas storage facilities and caused a halt in production at one of the largest gas fields in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. The Khurmor field is a main source of gas for power plants in the Kurdistan Region and had been targeted by attacks before.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said the increase in issuing and swiftly executing death sentences in Iran is not the decision of a few judges but an organized policy from the top of the regime. He added that this policy is led by Ebrahim Raisi, head of the judiciary, who repeatedly emphasizes faster issuance and execution of sentences. He called Ebrahim Raisi the new Khalkhali of the system.

Navid Mohibi said Prince Reza Pahlavi's ability to mobilize Iranians abroad has strengthened his political position. He added that the gathering of Iranians in Frankfurt and other cities could influence Western politicians and highlight Reza Pahlavi's role in the transition period. Mohibi also said that embassy closures alone do not lead to regime change, but combined with targeted sanctions and pursuing human rights violators, they could impose heavy political and diplomatic costs on the Islamic Republic.

Israel's Channel 13 reported that Admiral Brad Cooper, commander of the US Central Command (CENTCOM), has supported resuming war with the Islamic Republic. Cooper believes a third round of US attacks, including targeting bridges, power plants, and economic infrastructure, could change the positions of the Islamic Republic, and he has conveyed this view to senior US government officials. This report was published as the Israeli army prepares for the arrival of the third US aircraft carrier in the region.

Naser Karami, a climatologist and environmental expert, said drought and floods are not contradictory; rather, drought increases the risk of floods by destroying vegetation and soil structure. He added that changes in rainfall patterns in Iran have caused precipitation to occur more as severe floods, with water quickly becoming inaccessible. Karami also pointed to flooding in Tehran's streets, citing uncontrolled construction development and weak runoff management infrastructure as factors making the capital vulnerable to heavy rains, and emphasized that dispersed responsibilities have hindered preventive actions.

Barak Ravid reported that Marco Rubio, Jared Kushner, and Steve Whitcaff were present in the phone call between the US President and Benjamin Netanyahu. The call was initiated by Netanyahu and the two sides discussed the Gaza peace plan and the war with the Islamic Republic.

Shayan Samiei, a national security expert, said Donald Trump is trying to compel the Islamic Republic to make concessions without entering a new war by combining military threats and negotiation offers. According to him, Trump's reference to deploying aircraft carrier groups and potential attack targets indicates that the military option remains on the table. Samiei added that the Islamic Republic is trying to reduce Washington's pressure by prolonging negotiations and hoping for the results of the US midterm elections, and he considered this approach a miscalculation by Tehran.

Amir Giti, a member of Iran International's editorial board, said that despite ongoing diplomatic efforts between Tehran and Washington, the option of a US military attack remains on the table. He added that military and economic pressure on the Islamic Republic continues, and the nuclear issue remains Donald Trump's red line. According to him, if disagreements over the nuclear program persist, Washington could use its military capabilities stationed in the region.

Israel's Channel 13 reported that CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper, in a message to senior Israeli army commanders, supported the start of a new round of US military attacks against the Islamic Republic. According to the report, Cooper believes that the third round of US attacks, including targeting bridges, power plants, and economic infrastructure of Iran, could change the Islamic Republic's positions.

Bloomberg reported that Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, criticized the positions of the Islamic Republic in negotiations to end the war, saying Tehran's demands have so far been unacceptable and in some cases "shocking and ridiculous." Rubio also defended Donald Trump's approach, saying Trump was not elected to ignore the threat of Iran and leave it to the next president. He emphasized that Trump confronted this threat to ensure the security of American citizens, not for his personal interests.

Rainfall over the past 48 hours in Tehran and Qom has created unusual scenes. In Tehran, the entrance to the bridge from the Qeytarieh side has faced flooding. In Qom, an underpass has turned into a pool of water, and municipal forces used suction vehicles to evacuate the water.

Donald Trump said on the program "60 Minutes" that he does not intend to escalate the war with the Islamic Republic after the midterm elections because he sees no reason to do so. He added that Tehran is close to an agreement but the election results have given new hope to the Islamic Republic. Trump emphasized that if he had to decide again about attacking Iran, his answer would be "a definite yes."

The Middle East Spectator claimed that Ali Al-Zaidi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, warned Shiite armed groups in a closed-door meeting that military support for the Islamic Republic in the event of a new war would lead to widespread arrests of the commanders of these groups. The Islamic Resistance group in Iraq threatened that any action to arrest the leaders of Shiite groups would lead to the fall of the Iraqi government. It was also reported that the Iraqi Prime Minister said the US has plans for a ground attack on Iran from Iraqi territory.

Donald Trump said Washington has won the war against the Islamic Republic and the only issue now is whether to end the war "right now or later." He added that the US might wait because some of Iran's neighbors prefer the current situation to continue. Trump also said the US can target Iran's bridges and power plants but prefers not to because rebuilding these infrastructures takes years and puts heavy pressure on the people.

Donald Trump described the US economic statistics as "excellent" in an interview with CBS's "60 Minutes," but admitted his administration had failed to convey its message about the economy to the public. The interview took place hours after a US employment report showed better-than-expected results. A CBS News poll shows three-quarters of voters rated the economy as "bad" or "not very good," and 70% voted for Democratic candidates in the House elections.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, admitted that his administration was too harsh in enforcing immigrant deportation policies. He said his immigration policies have both benefited and harmed him politically. Trump expressed willingness to cooperate with congressional Democrats on immigration issues.

In an interview with CBS's 60 Minutes about the midterm elections, Trump said that people did not like the war, were unhappy with high gasoline prices, and there is strong dissatisfaction with Israel.
Donald Trump announced that he intends to use his pardon power broadly and pardon many people by the end of his presidential term.

Donald Trump said he spends almost no time reviewing his personal assets and his sons are responsible for running his company. He denied Forbes' report about the increase in his net worth and said his investments focus on broad market indices. Trump also spoke about Air Force pilots' accounts of unidentified flying objects, describing them as "very strange."

Anthony Albanese, Prime Minister of Australia, said he feels disgust toward the Islamic Republic regime and emphasized that the people of Iran will determine their own future. He announced his intention to discuss ending the war with Iran with Donald Trump on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit in Manila. The Australian government seeks a ceasefire, an end to the war through negotiation, and prevention of tolls on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

Amir Giti, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said that in the Monday meeting between Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Qatar's Prime Minister, and Donald Trump, President of the United States, proposals from the Islamic Republic to prevent the continuation of military operations or to achieve a ceasefire might be raised. He added that Trump is trying to avoid an immediate decision for military action and give diplomacy another chance.

The 16th Bita Award for Iranian Arts was presented to Sima Bina, a prominent singer and researcher of Iranian regional music, at Stanford University in the USA. The award was given in recognition of Sima Bina's more than six decades of efforts to preserve and expand Iran's musical heritage.

Dozens of Iranians living in Calgary, Canada, marched on the occasion of the Friedrich Naumann Foundation's Freedom Award being given to the people of Iran. Participants expressed support for Prince Reza Pahlavi, commemorated those who died in the January protests, and protested the ongoing executions in Iran.

Kayhan newspaper wrote that the imposed war has not ended and the Islamic Republic is still in the middle of this war. The newspaper referred to unity and solidarity around Mojtaba Khamenei and wrote that the Islamic Republic has managed to have the upper hand. Kayhan also mentioned the requirements of victorious endurance in this war, including a more offensive military approach and confronting enemy infiltration.

Abolfazl Sedaghat, a 20-year-old protester, along with Matin Farnian and Vahid Khodrikhah, have been sentenced to death on charges of "waging war against God" by the Mashhad Revolutionary Court. In a separate case in Shandiz, with death sentences issued for Ali Zaghi and Ilya Akbari, the number of those sentenced to death reached six. The judiciary executed three protesters from Dey month in Karaj on Sunday.

Mohammad Ghaedi, a lecturer in international relations, referring to the statements of Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, about Tehran's "unacceptable" demands, said that the Islamic Republic has not backed down from its previous demands even after the midterm elections, and the hope for a change in Tehran's position has not materialized. He added that Rubio considers the continuation of the naval blockade as a way to increase pressure, which might change the calculations of the Islamic Republic and the conditions for reaching an agreement.

Hossein Mohibi, spokesperson for the IRGC, said that no war mines have been cleared in the Strait of Hormuz and this claim is outright false. He added that no one dares to enter the Strait of Hormuz to clear mines. Mohibi also questioned how the US controls the Strait of Hormuz while several incidents happen daily to ships there.

The Indo-Pacific Defense Forum military magazine reported that China and Russia, despite claiming neutrality, support the Islamic Republic's war. According to the magazine, Russia has helped Tehran by providing satellite information and military and cyber cooperation, while China has assisted by supplying military equipment and purchasing Iranian oil. The report also mentioned trilateral cooperation between the Islamic Republic, China, and Russia in drone production.

Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, said Washington's actions in the region are "completely defensive" and if American forces or commercial ships are threatened, they will act to defend themselves. He considered the Islamic Republic's acquisition of nuclear weapons dangerous and unacceptable for the whole world and said Trump took responsibility for an action that previous presidents had failed to carry out.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said if Qatar's mediation realistically addresses the demands of both sides and focuses negotiations on the nuclear file, there is a possibility of progress in talks. He added that the Islamic Republic's demand to end all regional conflicts is not resolvable in talks with the US. Akbarin also said the Republican defeat in the midterm elections does not mean the end of Trump or the party, but the Islamic Republic believes it can prevent another attack by insisting on its positions.

The Human Rights Organization for Sports expressed concern in an open letter to the Asian Football Confederation about the death sentence issued for footballer Ehsan Hosseinipour Hesarlu, the imprisonment of Amir Reza Nasrazadani, and the arbitrary detention of several members of Iran's football community, calling for immediate action to protect their lives and safety. The organization highlighted violations of the right to a fair trial, denial of access to an independent lawyer, and restrictions on freedom of expression. It also emphasized the responsibility of the Asian Football Confederation and other sports bodies to support athletes facing the risk of arrest, imprisonment, and execution, urging immediate protection measures.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic, said in a press conference on Tuesday, 18 Aban, that there is no difference between the parties for Iran because it has been hurt by both political factions in the US. He described Tehran's demands as logical and said the US must stop sanctions, naval blockade, and economic expulsion operations to start negotiations. Baqaei also stated that if the US meets the Islamic Republic's demands, security will return to the region within two days, and Iran's two-day plan remains on the table.

According to a report by Harana News Agency, some general crime prisoners in Tehran Grand Prison have been transferred to the political prisoners' section and involved in internal order management under the title "security." Assigning guarding and security duties to prisoners is prohibited by the executive regulations of the Prisons Organization. Informed sources have also reported violent confrontations and threats against some prisoners, including the beating of Seyed Mehdi Hosseini, a detainee from the December 1404 protests.

Los Angeles Lakers defeated Detroit Pistons 121-116 without their injured star Luka Doncic, securing their top position in the Western Conference. Austin Reaves led the team with 43 points, 5 rebounds, and 4 assists. Walker Kessler contributed 12 points, 16 rebounds, and 3 blocks in the final moments to ensure the Lakers' victory.
A video received by Iran International shows the poor condition of the dormitory at Gorgan University after the rain on the evening of Sunday, 17 Aban.

The father of Paria Mehrmand, a 15-year-old basketball player injured in the overturning of the Sahar Academy team bus, reported the crushing of his daughter's leg and severe damage to its arteries and criticized the team's travel conditions, asking: "Who will be responsible to the families?" Also, the sister of another injured player said her sister was re-hospitalized due to severe pain after discharge. Families have demanded accountability from officials regarding this incident.
A video received by Iran International shows severe flooding in the streets of Gonbad Kavus city on the evening of Sunday, 17 Aban.
A bookstore in Tehran was sealed due to "non-compliance with Islamic norms." This was reported by the HRANA news agency. An informed source confirmed this news.

According to reports, dental costs in Iran are high, with each tooth extraction costing 6 million Tomans and root canal treatment 12 to 15 million Tomans. The prices of some medications, such as "Migrakim" and "Amoxicillin," have also significantly increased. Health insurance has excluded some medications and services from coverage, and diabetic patients are facing difficulties in obtaining their medicines.
Videos received by Iran International show flooding entering public streets of Bushehr on Sunday, 17 Aban after rainfall.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial board, said that Donald Trump's statements about continuing economic pressure, negotiation, and the possibility of attacking Iran's infrastructure are pursued simultaneously and are not contradictory. He added that the Islamic Republic fears a renewed uprising of the people and hopes to get through the remaining two years of Trump's administration. He believes the regime is deluded about achieving a "win-win" agreement and that the current process is against national interests and leads to another war.

The head of the judiciary in Isfahan province announced the decision to block social media pages of bloggers and popular individuals. According to Jafari, those whose published content falls under categories such as actions against national security, public security, and public norms will face page blocking and legal prosecution. These statements indicate an expansion of judicial oversight over users and bloggers and a possible restriction of freedom of expression in cyberspace.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the recent US attacks on southern Iran can be seen as initial waves of an operation to weaken and destroy the Islamic Republic's air defenses. He added this operation could be to facilitate the passage of ships through the Strait of Hormuz or prepare the field for broader air or even ground operations. Aghaei said the US used mostly inexpensive drones and Trump tries to end the war with less cost in favor of the US.
A video received by Iran International shows that the old Qazvin to Rasht road was flooded after rain on the evening of Sunday, 17 Aban.

Hossein Kermanpour, director general of public relations at the Ministry of Health, said the health system is prepared to face potential consequences of an attack on nuclear facilities and emergency and treatment measures have been planned. He advised people not to look at the explosion light and to seek shelter in a safe place as soon as possible. He also warned that taking iodine tablets without official instructions may harm the thyroid gland.

On Monday, 18 Aban, a group of retired telecommunications workers held a protest in the cities of Kermanshah and Isfahan. The protesting retirees demanded the full implementation of regulation 89/24, adjustment of salaries, and attention to their livelihood and medical issues.

Nima Dadgostar, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said Trump, in an interview with the program "60 Minutes," accepted part of JD Vance's assessment about voters' dissatisfaction with the war and rising living costs, but emphasized that if he could go back, he would make the same decision regarding the attack on Iran. Trump also spoke about excessive strictness towards some undocumented immigrants and expressed readiness to negotiate with Democrats to find a solution.

Messages received by Iran International indicate continued drug price increases, shortages, and removal of some drugs from insurance coverage. A diabetic citizen said the price of his needed Iranian medicine has quadrupled in two months. Another citizen said he spends over five million tomans monthly on medicine, and the price of his seizure medication increased by 200,000 tomans in one week.
Videos sent to Iran International show that a group of retired employees of Bank Saderat gathered in Tehran on Sunday, 17 Aban to pursue their demands.

Donald Trump said his offer to Dana White to become White House spokesperson was not serious and was just a joke. Trump said Dana liked the idea and described her as amazing. White said she is already busy and did not comment on accepting the position.

Aban (Zeinab) Mousavi and her brother Hassan Mousavi, two citizens arrested in connection with the protests of Dey 1404, have been held in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad for over eight months in judicial uncertainty. They face charges including "moharebeh" and no court has been held to address their charges so far. Temporary release on bail has also not been possible for them.

Hamidreza Goodarzi, representative of Aligudarz in the parliament, said that decisions about enriched uranium are made at the highest level of the country, and according to him, they will not deliver uranium under any circumstances. He added that if necessary, enrichment will be raised above 60 percent, and the Supreme National Security Council must decide on exiting the NPT to prevent the presence of IAEA inspectors. Goodarzi also said the enemy uses negotiations whenever it needs to breathe artificially.

Today, Monday, a group of workers from the National Iranian Steel Industrial Group gathered in the factory premises in Ahvaz. The protesters cited unpaid wage arrears, uncertainty in production status, and neglect of livelihood problems as reasons for holding this gathering.

Halvash news agency reported that a number of gas tanker drivers who have loaded their cargo for transfer to the Rimdan and Pishin borders of Pakistan remain uncertain at the Star of the Persian Gulf oil refinery in Bandar Abbas and have not been allowed to leave customs. A trade official also reported the stoppage of dozens of ships in northern ports and a threefold increase in maritime transport costs in the Caspian Sea.

Ziba Adeli, the technical director of the Sahar Academy women's basketball team, reported that 11 people were injured in the team's bus overturn accident and said that three players were injured in the spine area and the team may not be able to continue its presence in the Premier League. The team members were supposed to return from Khorramshahr to Tehran by train at 18:00 on Saturday, but due to a landslide and train cancellation, they traveled by bus which overturned near Shush. Paria Mehrmand and Somayeh Sabetzadeh suffered fractures and require surgery.

Today, continuing protests by retired telecommunications workers, some retirees gathered in the cities of Zanjan and Rasht and demanded attention to their demands. These gatherings were held in protest against ongoing livelihood problems and the unmet demands of retirees.

A video received by Iran International shows a funeral for a person titled "Unknown Martyr" held in the campus of Azad University of Karaj, and the attendees of this ceremony are shouting "Heydar, Heydar."

According to a report published by ILNA, some employed women face administrative and insurance problems in receiving their claims from the Social Security Organization and are forced to pursue legal action. A woman filed a complaint to increase the duration of maternity leave and receive full pay for this period from the Social Security Department of Khorasan Razavi province, and the judicial authorities ruled in her favor. Simin Yaghoubi, a women's labor rights activist, stated that delays in payment, incorrect calculations, and restrictive interpretations of laws lead to the violation of insured women's rights and weaken public trust in the social security system.
